about: World 8, Thermo Track: a three-lane runner. Change lanes, jump and slide with the keys, swipes, or your body (webcam). changes = energy changes that float above the track; exo = true for exothermic (gives out heat), false for endothermic (takes in heat); dh = enthalpy change in kJ/mol where given (negative means exothermic). questions = gates across the track; run through the lane with the right answer (answer = 0, 1 or 2). In each level, collect says which kind of change to grab ('exo' or 'endo'); the other kind must be dodged. obstacles = how many barriers to jump, slide under or dodge. speed = track speed (1 is normal).

wood.label: Burning wood
wood.why: Combustion gives out heat and light, so burning wood is exothermic.

freeze.label: Water freezing
freeze.why: Water gives out energy as its molecules lock into ice, so freezing is exothermic.

respire.label: Respiration
respire.why: Your cells break down glucose and release energy, so respiration is exothermic.

warmer.label: Hand warmer
warmer.why: Iron powder rusting inside a hand warmer releases heat: exothermic.

condense.label: Steam condensing
condense.why: Steam gives out energy as it turns back into liquid water, so condensing is exothermic. That is why steam burns are so painful.

neutral.label: Acid + alkali
neutral.why: Neutralisation gives out heat: the mixture gets warmer, so it is exothermic.

melt.label: Ice melting
melt.why: Ice takes in heat from its surroundings to melt, so melting is endothermic.

boil.label: Water boiling
boil.why: Boiling takes in energy to pull the water molecules apart, so it is endothermic.

photo.label: Photosynthesis
photo.why: Plants absorb light energy to make glucose, so photosynthesis is endothermic.

coldpack.label: Cold pack
coldpack.why: Ammonium nitrate dissolving in water takes in heat, so the pack feels cold: endothermic.

sweat.label: Sweat drying
sweat.why: Evaporating sweat takes heat from your skin, which cools you down: endothermic.

bake.label: Baking a cake
bake.why: Baking needs a steady supply of heat from the oven, so it is endothermic.

ch4.label: CH₄ burns
ch4.why: ΔH = −890 kJ/mol. A negative ΔH means energy is given out: exothermic.

naoh.label: NaOH dissolves
naoh.why: ΔH = −44 kJ/mol. Negative, so dissolving sodium hydroxide warms the water: exothermic.

icemelt.label: Ice melts
icemelt.why: ΔH = +6 kJ/mol. Positive, so energy is taken in: endothermic.

waterboil.label: Water boils
waterboil.why: ΔH = +41 kJ/mol at 100 °C. Positive, so endothermic.

caco3.label: CaCO₃ splits
caco3.why: ΔH = +178 kJ/mol. Breaking down limestone needs strong heating: endothermic.

nh4no3.label: NH₄NO₃ dissolves
nh4no3.why: ΔH = +26 kJ/mol. Positive, so the water gets colder: endothermic.

breakbond.why: Breaking bonds always takes in energy, because atoms must be pulled apart against their attraction.

makebond.why: Making bonds always gives out energy. Exothermic reactions release more energy making bonds than they used breaking them.

exoprod.q: In an exothermic reaction, the products have…
exoprod.why: The products have less energy than the reactants; the difference is given out as heat, so ΔH is negative.

exosurr.q: An exothermic reaction makes its surroundings…
exosurr.why: Exothermic reactions give out heat, so the surroundings (the test tube, the water, your hand) get warmer.

endosign.q: For an endothermic reaction, ΔH is…
endosign.why: Endothermic reactions take in energy, so the products have more energy than the reactants and ΔH is positive.

activation.why: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need for a reaction to start. Even exothermic reactions need it, like a match to light paper.
